text.p: Italian engineering group Finmeccanica and Britain's General Electric Co Plc will set up a defence systems joint venture and take minority stakes in some of their respective defence operations, Finmeccanica said in a statement on Thursday.
"Finmeccanica and the General Electric Company have reached a preliminary deal for broad strategic cooperation in the defence sector," the Italian state controlled company said.

At the heart of the deal is an equally-owned joint venture which will work on missile systems, naval systems, ground-based radar, command and control systems and air traffic control systems, Finmeccanica said.

"As of now we have agreed the construction of an equally owned joint-venture for research, planning, production and marketing of the majority of the groups' present output," the Finmeccanica statement said.

In addition GEC-Marconi will take a minority stake in Alenia Defence avionics business, a Finmeccanica unit, while Alenia will take a minority stake in GEC-Marconi's armament and armoured car operations.
GEC and Finmeccanica signed a memorandum of understanding to explore opportunities for defence collaboration in March.
The Italian group, which is contolled by state holding Iri, said the deal's fine print would be sorted out by the end of the year.
